actual_source_title: Classification accuracy of TMS for the diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment

blind_codes.note: blind codes of the pack PDF (Amato et al. 2024), which is not P-263's actual source

judgement_basis: non-blind check against the actual source of the P-263 row and summary block, Benussi et al. 2021 (Brain Stimulation)

Task_Type.reason: Benussi 2021 chains three binary random-forest classifiers (MCI vs HC, then MCI-FTD vs MCI-non-FTD, then MCI-AD vs MCI-DLB) to assign each subject to one of four classes. T3 fits that multi-class structure including HC, but not its staging meaning, since the classes are aetiologies rather than stages. T1 (the first-level MCI vs HC classifier, accuracy 0.84) and T4 (aetiological MCI subtype) are the alternative readings.
Task_Type.quote: As reported in Fig. 3, a hierarchical series of subsequent 3 binary (two-groups) and independent classifiers were employed: i) MCI vs HC; ii) MCI-FTD vs MCI-non-FTD (MCI-AD or MCI-DLB), iii) MCI-AD vs MCI-DLB.

Category.reason: The only analysed data are TMS paired-pulse measures recorded by EMG (neurophysiology); CSF, PET and DaTSCAN enter only as diagnostic reference labels.

Validation_Type.reason: Two readings. V2: the new classifier was trained and validated with 5-fold CV within the same multicentre cohort, and Table 2 is labelled '5-fold cross-validation'. V3: a previously published classifier trained on about 650 dementia patients was applied to this new MCI cohort, but the paper does not show that cohort came from different institutions.
Validation_Type.quote: By computing a new classifier, both trained and validated on the current cohort of MCI patients, classification indices with 5-fold-cross validation adjusted for age, sex and center, showed even higher accuracy (ranging from 0.83 to 0.93)

Sample_N_Approx.reason: The abstract prints '160 participants were included'. Results state that 160 were assessed for eligibility, 7 were excluded, and 153 (64 MCI-AD + 28 MCI-FTD + 14 MCI-DLB + 47 HC) were analysed. The registry uses the enrolled figure.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: Thus, one hundred fifty-three subjects were considered in the present analysis.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Italian multicentre TMS cohort; no ADNI data.

Task_Type.reason: Amato 2024 trains a binary HC vs MCI classifier (random forest, F1 0.95) and has no multi-class classifier.
Task_Type.quote: We then tested several machine learning algorithms to perform a binary classification between HC subjects and MCI patients based on the EEG features identified in the previous section.

Validation_Type.reason: Nested cross-validation in a single-centre sample.

Sample_N_Approx.quote: we collected electroencephalography (EEG) recordings at rest from participants in healthy (HC, n = 17), subjective cognitive decline (SCD, n = 58), and mild cognitive impairment (MCI, n = 44) conditions

notes: The census row for P-263 is consistent with its own paper (Benussi 2021); the defect is the PDF map. The Amato 2024 EEG paper is not a corpus study, so its disagreement with the row is not a registry error, and it should not be counted as three registry errors. The map also assigns the Benussi PDF to P-863 under the title 'Medical Journey of Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment...'; that entry should be checked. Minor: the P-263 summary block writes '160 subjects: 64 MCI-AD, 28 MCI-FTD, 14 MCI-DLB, 47 healthy controls', which sums to 153. Status check after the concurrent commit f028bc9 (2026-09-27 11:54, 63 map rows repaired): the P-263 entry is still the unrepaired formula-unverified Amato path, and P-863 still points to the Benussi PDF under the 'Medical Journey...' title.
